outcome: anal incontinence (including flatus incontinence and urgency)
cohort: 862 healthy first-time mothers (primiparas) from two Norwegian hospitals.
finding: In most first-time mothers with postpartum anal incontinence, the onset of incontinence was before delivery, with incontinence in late pregnancy and young age increasing the risk of persistence.
mod_finding: Occipitoposterior presentation was the only delivery-related factor that increased the risk of postpartum anal incontinence (OR 1.8, 95% CI 1.0-3.4); other delivery-related factors did not.
